text_blocks.snippet: James Watson and Francis Crick discovered the double-helix structure of DNA in 1953, relying heavily on the crucial X-ray diffraction data produced by Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins.
James Watson and Francis Crick: Built the physical double-helix model at Cambridge University and published the landmark paper in 1953.
Rosalind Franklin: Captured "Photograph 51," an exceptional X-ray diffraction image that provided the vital clues about the helical shape of DNA.
Maurice Wilkins: Shared Franklin's X-ray images with Watson without her direct knowledge, aiding the modeling process.
Erwin Chargaff: Discovered that adenine pairs with thymine and cytosine pairs with guanine, which informed the base-pairing rules of the model. Nature +4
Watson, Crick, and Wilkins later shared the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery, while Franklin had passed away four years prior.
